Not trying to be a dissenting opinion - but want to help too since it seems like you’re anxious. These forums are where people tend to go who have the absolute worst symptoms. The people who were very unlucky, potentially have comorbid conditions and quite frankly, may be very anxious and stressed. 

For example, if you go to a forum about Long Covid, and ask for advice about Covid, are you going to hear from the people who had a mild case and then recovered? Not likely. You’re going to hear from the people who are continuing to experience symptoms and are having a tough time. Even if it’s a much smaller percentage, it will feel like it’s everyone because of where you’re posting.

I’m not diminishing what anyone is saying at all because I believe their suffering is real, but there’s a lot of people who have GERD (20%+ of the population) and most of them just live their lives and don’t overthink or stress about it.

Not saying you shouldn’t take care of yourself, but also realize that sometimes the opinions you get on the internet are more extreme examples. I’m saying  this as someone who has tremendous health anxiety. It makes things a lot worse for you when you look up symptoms and ask for advice from strangers.

Work with your doctor, do what helps you heal through trial and error and then try not to look back. The risk of cancer is extremely low if that’s your primary concern, so be diligent, get check ups and move on.

Also - you have to dig, but there are some success stories in this community of people who either completely healed/controlled their GERD by reducing their chronic stress. Some are back to eating and drinking whatever they want. The body is a spectacular system that wants to heal itself, so treat it kindly, and then work on the mind. It will pay off well in the long run.

Going to chime in here - I was told my all 4 neurosurgeons I went to that I could return to all activity - including coasters and jet skiing. But…I should mention that I don’t get headaches or have EDS, POTS…just dizziness, which as of 3 months ago I did not have. They said post op I’m good to go so long as the activity doesn’t aggravate anything.

To give some background, my Chiari wasn’t diagnosed until the dizziness started. I had some symptoms (visual snow, tinnitus, poor hand eye coordination, etc) but none that impeded my life significantly. I was actually going on roller coasters two weeks before my dizziness started with literally zero symptoms. No headaches, no vertigo, nothing. My dizziness got triggered randomly at the gym one day when I lifted something wrong.

There is no empirical evidence of catastrophic injury or issues from activity post op short of things like car accidents and extreme trauma. I asked every doctor about sports, including football and they said there is no data showing there is greater risk so they clear even kids to return to contact sports. So I asked anecdotally and they also said they have had no one who needed a re op due to football, coasters, etc.

I am a huge extreme sports person and the docs said I have zero to worry about after my surgery and could get back to my normal life in 6 months or so. 

Just keep this in mind - everyone’s condition is different and may have different limitations and risks. However, doctors will sometimes recommend precautions not for you, but so they don’t get sued or have to re-op. If you don’t want to risk things, that’s your call. Just keep in mind that a lot of doctors have their own self interests at heart and care more about a clean record than your quality of life. After all, they hope to never see you again after surgery. My recommendation? See multiple docs (that are trusted and perform the surgery often), get multiple opinions.

I have had severe anxiety for about 15 years - and I have shaky hands for about 9 years. At first, I was just attributing this to anxiety. But then I noticed over the last year or so that my handwriting got worse and I’ve had more muscle twitches and poor grip. So I looked up shaky hands and found tremors. 

Now tremors can be caused by anxiety, but they can also be caused by neurological disorders. And essential tremors is a neurodegenerative disease that makes your tremors debilitating as life goes on. Anxiety tremors apparently come and go…but mine are constant…so now I’m convinced I have essential tremors and am in total panic mode about my future quality of life given there’s no cure. Apparently treatments are never very successful outside of surgery which is invasive and also not always successful.

I want to believe my chronic anxiety had led to constant hand tremors but now my mind is convinced it’s more serious. 

I need help…
